subject: Distance from "the line", or where you happen to be at the time?

messages.author: d72c483eb6ae6ddb
messages.subject: Distance from "the line", or where you happen to be at the time?
parts:
G'day Distance samplers,

On line transects, is the perpendicular distance to an animal taken from =
the predetermined "line", or from where you happen to be at the time of s=
ighting?? I've had conflicting statistical advice on this.

(We spotlight for ground-dwelling marsupials on islands. Our transect li=
nes are marked out by reflective tape, but we only walk them once a year,=
so some of the markers inevitably fall down and we walk "the line" by GP=
S until we can see the next reflector post to aim for. This, together wi=
th patches of bush that we have to go around rather than through, means w=
e sometimes stray tens of metres off "the line". This also means we coul=
d be missing animals on the actual line. I know it would be ideal to wal=
k on "the line" at all times, but it is reality that we don't.)

Linda
